messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate and p99 latency from route /v1/generate (eu-west-1). 5xx = 18% over 1m, retries spiking. Pager -> @oncall-jess. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood/1779501234

oncall-jess: on it. grabbing logs and routing traces now. assigning SRE.

sre-ryan: I see a big cluster of requests failing locally then falling back cross-region to us-east-1 where a larger model variant is being used. p99 jumps from 300ms -> 3s after failover.

alice-mlops: why is fallback picking the 16b variant? routing policy should prefer same-arch smaller variants. pulling policy history.

eng-platform-lee: grabbing routing policy: here's the active snippet we just rolled at 14:58 UTC:
```yaml
routing_policies:
  - route: /v1/generate
    primary_model_family: gpt-medium
    fallback_order:
      - model: gptx-16b-quant
      - model: gpt-medium-8b
    cross_region_fallback: true
    region_preference: prefer-local
```
looks like fallback_order was misordered in the last rollout (ops-review change).

maria-product: customers calling in — token usage exploded for some orgs because longer model = more tokens per response. not good.

customersupport-ken: Acme SE says they saw timeouts at ~14:17 and their client retried aggressively which made things worse. they reported 5-10x request fanout.

sre-ryan: confirmed in traces: client retry header X-Client-Retry: 3 and backoff 200ms, server side failover returns 503 quickly and client retries, which lands to smart-router -> triggers cross-region failover which spins up more replicas in us-east-1. loop amplifies traffic.

eng-platform-lee: observed behavior: client retries + router doing failover = amplification. router does not currently decrement retry budget when switching backend. so a single client retry became multiple backend attempts across regions.

alice-mlops: logs: snippet from router trace:
```
[14:16:52] request id=abc123 route=/v1/generate -> local pool returned 503 (model-oom)
[14:16:52] router decision -> fallback to us-east-1/model=gptx-16b-quant
[14:16:52] request forwarded
[14:16:52] client retries (attempt 2) -> new request id=abc124 -> router again decides to fallback -> additional forward to us-east-1
```
This shows duplicate forwarded attempts.

oncall-jess: Priority now: 1) stop cross-region amplification, 2) reduce incoming retries, 3) restore healthy local capacity.

eng-platform-lee: temporary mitigations I can push right now:
- flip cross_region_fallback -> false for /v1/generate
- set fallback_order to prefer same-arch smaller models only
- apply per-client low-level rate limit 10r/s and circuit-breaker after 5 503s in 30s
I can roll the change in 60s if no objections.

maria-product: please do it, customers are impacted. notify support.

customersupport-ken: contacting top 5 affected customers now (Acme, BlueCo, FinServX, Shoply). will post status update.

eng-platform-lee: rolling config now -> `platformctl apply-config --route /v1/generate --set cross_region_fallback=false --set fallback_order=[gpt-medium-8b,gpt-medium-4b]`

eng-platform-lee: config rollout started. gradually pushing to edge proxies. watching.

sre-ryan: can we also inject a header that tells clients to stop retrying? we can mark 503 responses with `Retry-After: 10` and `X-RW-Retry-Suppress: 1` to discourage immediate client retries.

oncall-jess: good idea. eng-platform-lee can you add that to the gateway response mapping?

eng-platform-lee: adding mapping now. command: `gatewayctl patch /routes/generate --set response_headers={'Retry-After':'10','X-RW-Retry-Suppress':'1'}`

incident-bot: Deploy started for gateway patch (deploy-4567). CI: green. Rolling to 50% in 30s.

alice-mlops: also coordinating a fast scale up of local model pool to handle backlog instead of failing over. spinning up additional replicas for gpt-medium-8b. `k8s scale --replicas=10 deployment/gpt-medium-8b-eu`

sre-ryan: observing metrics: after config flip and gateway patch, p99 latency dropping from 3.2s -> 600ms in 2m. 5xx rate down from 18% -> 3% and trending.

customersupport-ken: update posted to customers: "We observed elevated latency and retries; temporary mitigation applied; we will follow up with root cause and mitigations next week." :white_check_mark:

maria-product: rough impact numbers? estimated affected orgs: 5 high-severity, ~120 orgs with transient errors. Billing spike alert for a few customers—we'll need credits.

oncall-jess: handing over to @oncall-maya for midnight shift. summary:
- root cause: routing policy misordered fallback -> cross-region fallback to wrong model variant + client retry amplification.
- mitigations applied: cross-region fallback disabled, gateway retry-suppress headers, per-client rate limits, scaled local pool.
- current status: stable, latency and errors falling, no new customer escalations in last 10m.

oncall-maya: taking over. I will monitor for next 2 hours and start incident writeup. please paste any logs/links.

sre-ryan: saving traces for postmortem. link: https://traces.redwood/trace/abc123?incident=1779501234

eng-platform-lee: opened rollback PR to reorder fallback permanently and add a unit test to prevent cross-arch fallback being first. PR: https://git.redwood/plat/routing/changes/789

maria-product: create postmortem ticket and customer compensation plan. I'll coordinate with finance and CSMs.

incident-bot: Incident severity -> P1 (escalated). Postmortem requested. Creator: oncall-jess. SLA impact: some requests exceeded latency SLA; select customers experienced degraded service.

customersupport-ken: final note: Acme accepted credits and is ok with proposed follow-up. thanks all. :pray:

oncall-maya: I will keep monitoring and will add notes to the PM ticket. passing to ops-runbook for detailed RCA later.

sre-ryan: action items before close:
- [ ] merge routing PR and add CI guard
- [ ] add router logic to decrement retry budget when failover happens
- [ ] add circuit-breaker to prevent cross-region scale on transient 503s
- [ ] write customer-facing postmortem and credits plan

incident-bot: Incident marked stable at 1779504060. Auto-close scheduled in 24h if no regressions.
